title: We Knew the Terms
style: Adult contemporary pop with a relaxed reggae groove and polished late-2010s production. Midtempo one-drop rhythm, tight rim-click and warm rounded bass, clean offbeat electric guitar, restrained keys, and subtle atmospheric pads. Verses stay conversational and intimate, opening into a memorable, emotionally assured chorus; add light harmony layers in the final chorus and a neat, understated outro. Female lead vocal with a natural British accent, clear diction, warm and poised delivery. Clean radio-ready mix with organic groove and controlled low end.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
April rain on London stone
A crowded pub, a name I’d known
Thomas asked, then listened close
No polished pitch, no practiced pose
We spoke until the morning thinned
He drove me home; we stayed in touch
A friendship found its steady pace
No grand design, no need to rush

[Chorus]
We knew the terms, we knew the room
A little space, a little truth
Across the miles, the years, the view
I kept my own; I welcomed you
No promises we couldn’t keep
Just honest words and trust that deep
From London out to Bogotá
We made a life that travelled far

[Verse 2]
Aachen, October, unhurried days
The road ran soft through border towns
Some things don’t need a name out loud
When both hearts know what’s settled down
Karim had been there years before
Since fourteen, steady, kind, discreet
He never asked beyond my yes
A friend who knew when not to reach

[Chorus]
We knew the terms, we knew the room
A little space, a little truth
Across the miles, the years, the view
I kept my own; I welcomed you
No promises we couldn’t keep
Just honest words and trust that deep
From London out to Bogotá
We made a life that travelled far

[Bridge]
Barcelona held a table wide
New York kept another place
Gabi, Fiona, familiar doors
A changing map, a constant grace
Diana teased; the talk stayed kind
Claire and Pilar, work and warmth
I never had to own the room
To feel at home among them all

[Final Chorus]
We knew the terms, we knew the room
A little space, a little truth
Across the miles, the years, the view
I kept my own; I welcomed you
No promises we couldn’t keep
Just honest words and trust that deep
From London out to Bogotá
We made a life that travelled far

[Outro]
A few close friends, a world between
And room to let each person be
